doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

title: What tradition means
summary: Responding to Albert Murray's idea, Glasper says tradition is change: honor the history but keep moving.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Now I’m going to ask one more question then you all get ready because I’m going to let you all get in here. I want to talk about tradition and continuity of tradition. I did a presentation here on the great writer about blues and jazz, Albert Murray. And one of the things he says in his book The Hero and the Blues is that of course tradition is that which continues. That’s obvious. But he says if the tradition is not — this is my paraphrase — renewed then the tradition can atrophy. So you actually need change for the tradition to remain alive.

A tradition is change also. You know what I mean? What is a tradition? When you think of a tradition as — that’s why people talk to me about that stuff, about you don’t even know what you’re talking about from the beginning, your question don’t even make sense. Why don’t you keep more of the tradition? Which tradition? Which era? Which one? The thirties? Because when the forties hit, that was something different. When the fifties hit, that was something different. When the sixties hit, each era looked back on the other era, or looked ahead at the other era like, “what are you doing? That’s not the tradition.” You know? They all did that. The thirties looked at the forties like what are you doing? The forties looked at the fifties, what are you doing? And like the sixties, what are you doing? That’s the tradition. If you’re not making the other era mad you’re not following the tradition. Your tradition is to piss you off.
Or in the academy they call it paradigm shifts.

Yeah, yeah, yeah, exactly. But that is the tradition. The tradition is to honor the history but not be held back by the history. And you keep it moving. You keep it moving. But you honor it and you know it’s there, you pay homage to it but you keep it moving.
Because that’s the only way to keep it alive. Miles said it. If it ain’t moving it’s dead. Period.
